summary: FR-001 to FR-015, US1 to US5, the declared seams and the Red lines for T002 to T006 (each names an existing test in the same commit as its implementation) are met, but the tree_digest seam is under direct test without a declared or confirmed seam (ENG-4), and the OpenCode and Codex procedures fall short of FR-012 and SC-006. Worktree: /Users/tenluap/Desktop/SourceCode/Personal/claude-factory-factory/018-live-conformance.

findings.summary: A task-required seam, bench.tree_digest, is put under direct test but is neither declared in the plan's test seams nor covered by the confirmed scope.
findings.evidence: ENG-4 and engineering.md 'Confirmed test scope': tasks.md T004 requires tree_digest tests ('tree_digest equals the data-model formula ... and changes when one byte changes'). test_bench.py:429-442 calls bench_module.tree_digest directly; it is also used as the oracle at lines 475 and 492. plan.md 'Test seams' declares three seams only (bench.py run CLI, bench.py score CLI, bench.checkout_provenance(path)); the plan.md 'Confirmed:' line and factory/relay/plan-Q1.md list the same three. tree_digest is not declared, so no current explicit acceptance covers this seam.
findings.fix: Stop under ENG-4 and report the missing seam. The orchestrator obtains fresh protected confirmation declaring bench.tree_digest(path) and its failure paths before the seam is tested. If that is not accepted, drop the direct tree_digest tests (test_bench.py:429-442) and check the formula through the declared run seam, using an expected hash computed inside the test from the data-model formula rather than bench_module.tree_digest.

findings.summary: FR-007 requires the installed factory revision in the provenance record, but the record holds only the skill path and a tree digest.
findings.evidence: spec.md FR-007 lists 'installed factory revision'; US4 AS5 says 'installed factory revision that cannot be determined'. installed_factory (bench.py:278-283) returns {skill_dir, digest} with no revision field. data-model.md installed_factory has the same shape, and research.md R5 records the substitution as a decision, so the code follows the plan while the spec wording is unmet.
findings.fix: Reconcile spec.md FR-007, Key Entities and US4 AS5 with research R5 and data-model.md through the spec owner. Either record a revision next to the digest (for example the installed factory_sha used by the improvement export, or 'unavailable') or amend the spec wording to 'installed factory digest'. Assert whichever field is chosen.

findings.summary: The OpenCode checklist does not state the PR leg or the resume and installed-baseline steps itself; it defers them to claude-code.md, against T008, FR-012, FR-014 and SC-006.
findings.evidence: tasks.md T008 requires 'same items as T007 for opencode run'; FR-012 requires the OpenCode checklist to state the FR-011 items; FR-014 requires the procedure to name tenluap/factory-golden-run-<date>; SC-006 requires a checklist path that needs no other source for resume or PR steps. opencode.md:38 reads 'Headless smoke, pause, kill, resume, installed baseline, PR leg: follow the same steps as claude-code.md'. grep finds 0 occurrences of 'factory-golden-run' in opencode.md (1 in claude-code.md).
findings.fix: Write the PR leg (private tenluap/factory-golden-run-<date>, created at trial time, kept as evidence), the resume step and the installed-baseline run into opencode.md itself so the checklist stands alone.

findings.summary: The Codex fallback that both checklists route the cross-harness leg to still has unfilled capability placeholders.
findings.evidence: codex.md:22 '<second>', codex.md:32 '<fill from adapters/codex/harness.md>', codex.md:33 '<enforced | disclosed limitation>', codex.md:34 '<fill from harness.md, or none>'. opencode.md:39 and claude-code.md:22 route the cross-harness fallback to golden-run/codex.md. FR-012 requires the Codex fallback for the cross-harness leg, and SC-006 requires a path a maintainer can follow without consulting another source; codex.md itself points to adapters/codex/harness.md.
findings.fix: Fill codex.md's invoke, enforcement, setup and resume-step notes from its harness file. If that is not possible yet, state in both checklists that the Codex fallback is not runnable and the cross-harness leg is blocked until it is.

findings.summary: Both checklists cite the internal task id 'T008', which a maintainer cannot resolve.
findings.evidence: claude-code.md:22 reads '(the Codex fallback is in golden-run/codex.md, see T008)'; opencode.md:22 has the same text. T008 is a tasks.md id, not a procedure step, so the checklist does not stand alone (SC-006).
findings.fix: Delete ', see T008' from both lines.

findings.summary: The T010 implementation commit has no Red line and no plan exemption, although tasks.md describes T010 as having no commit unit.
findings.evidence: ENG-2. Commit f6f2981, subject 'factory(implement): T010 final verification', changes only the tasks.md checkbox and has no 'Red:' line. plan.md declares no exemption for T010; tasks.md T010 reads 'no file change, no commit unit'. The commit changes no behaviour, so the ENG-2 trigger may not apply; the textual check still flags it.
findings.fix: Either record the T010 verification without the factory(implement) subject, or have plan.md declare T010 exempt because it changes no behaviour. No test is missing.

findings.summary: A non-UTF-8 git path or harness version output raises UnicodeDecodeError past the 'unavailable' handling and aborts the run before launch.
findings.evidence: FR-008: 'A provenance value that cannot be determined MUST be recorded as unavailable rather than abort the run.' checkout_provenance (bench.py:215-237) decodes git output inside a try that catches only OSError, CalledProcessError and TimeoutExpired. harness_version (bench.py:256-268) runs with text=True and catches only OSError and TimeoutExpired. UnicodeDecodeError escapes write_provenance; main() reports it as a ValueError and exits 1 before the harness launches. ENG-17 covers deliberate error handling.
findings.fix: Decode with errors='replace', or catch UnicodeDecodeError into the 'unavailable' fallback. A regression test adds an undeclared failure path, so obtain fresh seam confirmation first (ENG-4).

findings.summary: In checkout mode a missing render directory yields a valid-looking digest instead of 'unavailable'.
findings.evidence: data-model.md: 'A value that cannot be determined is the string unavailable.' write_provenance (bench.py:291) calls safe_digest(out/home/dist/<harness>) with no existence check. os.walk over a missing root yields nothing, so tree_digest (bench.py:240) returns the sha256 of the empty record stream. installed_factory (bench.py:278) checks existence first, so the two branches behave differently.
findings.fix: Check that the render directory exists and record 'unavailable' otherwise, as installed_factory does.

findings.summary: docs/benchmark.md still describes only --home and --out, and says the driver uses the installed factory, which is now true only without --from-checkout.
findings.evidence: docs/benchmark.md:16 lists 'Optional: --home ... --out ...' with no --model or --from-checkout. Lines 6-7 say the driver 'uses the installed factory skill, not an implicit install from this checkout'. The upstream live-conformance plan links this procedure. spec.md Q8 makes the golden-run checklists the procedure of record, so this is documentation drift rather than a missed requirement.
findings.fix: Add --model, --from-checkout and the provenance.json output to docs/benchmark.md, or point it at the golden-run checklists.
